summary: Zhu constructs the Witt vector affine Grassmannian as an ind-perfect algebraic space (Theorem 1.4), proves the geometric Satake equivalence in mixed characteristic (with a rational-coefficient Gelfand-trick proof of the commutativity constraint), identifies perfected Hodge-type Rapoport–Zink special fibres with affine Deligne–Lusztig varieties, and proves Rapoport's dimension formula (Theorem 3.1). Complete (cc-442dc5): every numbered statement is an item, every missing item is routed exactly once, and thirty-four findings are recorded. The Appendix A.3 statements E24–E27 are false as printed in their generality, and Appendix B's results are stated without proof (E34); the main theorems are unaffected. Not formalised.

items.statement: For pfp perfect X, choose finitely generated k-subfields K_i of each generic residue field whose perfections give that field. The corresponding weakly normal finite-presentation model is unique with these identifications.

api.name: Zhu17.A21.construct
api.statement: Construct sections whose generic values lie in the prescribed K_i.

api.name: Zhu17.A21.characterise
api.statement: Prove weak normality and the universal pushout property with the generic fields.

api.name: Zhu17.A21.transport
api.statement: Descend the construction along étale presentations.

uses.how: Provides canonical chosen deperfections.

items.name: Pfp perfect universal homeomorphism rigidity
items.statement: A separated universal homeomorphism between pfp perfect algebraic spaces is an isomorphism.

items.name: Morphisms descend to finite models
items.statement: Every morphism between pfp perfect algebraic spaces is the perfection of a morphism of finite-presentation models, after sufficiently many Frobenius twists of a model.

items.name: Perfectly proper morphism
items.statement: A morphism of pfp perfect algebraic spaces is perfectly proper if separated and universally closed.

api.name: Zhu17.A24.construct
api.statement: Package separatedness and universal closedness.

api.name: Zhu17.A24.characterise
api.statement: Characterize it by properness of every finite-presentation model.

api.name: Zhu17.A24.transport
api.statement: Prove stability under composition and base change in the pfp category.

uses.how: Distinguishes properness in perfect geometry from ordinary finite type.

items.name: Proper models characterize perfect properness
items.statement: For f between pfp perfect spaces, f is perfectly proper if and only if any/every finite-presentation model f′ is proper.

items.name: Perfect valuation criterion
items.statement: A map between pfp perfect algebraic spaces is perfectly proper exactly when its existence-and-uniqueness valuative criterion holds for all perfect valuation rings over k.

items.name: Connected proper fibres and functions
items.statement: For a surjective perfectly proper f between pfp perfect algebraic spaces with geometrically connected fibres, O_Y→f_*O_X is an isomorphism. Here the connected-fibre convention includes nonemptiness.

items.name: Vector bundles descend to models
items.statement: A finite-rank vector bundle on a pfp perfect algebraic space descends to a finite-presentation model after a Frobenius twist.

items.name: Relative Grassmann representability
items.statement: For a rank-n bundle E on pfp perfect X and 0≤i≤n, the functor of locally free rank-i quotients of E is represented by a perfect algebraic space perfectly proper over X.

items.name: Picard group of perfect projective space
items.statement: For n≥1, Pic((P^n_k)^perf)=Z[1/p], with distinguished O(1) and (Frob^-1)^*O(1)=O(1/p). For n=0 the Picard group is zero.

items.name: Perfect smoothness
items.statement: A map f:X→Y of pfp perfect algebraic spaces is perfectly smooth at x if étale charts factor it as an étale map to V×(A^n)^perf followed by projection.

api.name: Zhu17.A265.construct
api.statement: Construct the étale chart factorization at the specified point.

api.name: Zhu17.A265.characterise
api.statement: Track the local relative dimension n.

api.name: Zhu17.A265.transport
api.statement: Prove stability under base change and composition.

uses.how: Supplies orbit geometry and shifted smooth pullback.

items.name: Dense perfectly smooth locus
items.statement: Every pfp perfect algebraic space over perfect k has a dense open perfectly smooth subspace.

items.name: Smooth models of perfect groups
items.statement: Every pfp perfect group scheme over perfect k is the perfection of a smooth finite-type algebraic group.

items.name: Perfect affine torsors are étale locally trivial
items.statement: Every torsor under an affine pfp perfect k-group on a perfect algebraic space is étale locally trivial.

items.name: Affine perfect actions descend
items.statement: An action of an affine pfp perfect group H on an affine pfp perfect scheme X descends to an action of a smooth affine finite-type group H′ on an affine finite-type X′.

items.name: Free perfect affine action quotient
items.statement: For affine pfp perfect H acting freely on affine pfp perfect X, the fpqc quotient X/H is a pfp perfect algebraic space.

items.name: Separated free-action quotient
items.statement: Under A.29, if (act,pr2):H×X→X×X is a closed immersion, X/H is separated.

items.name: Finite-flat groupoid perfect quotient
items.statement: Let V⇉U be an equivalence relation of pfp perfect schemes arising by perfection from a finite locally free groupoid V′⇉U′ of quasiprojective k-schemes. Then U/V is represented by a pfp perfect scheme.

items.name: Ferrand flatness descent over perfect rings
items.statement: Let R→S be an injective integral map of perfect rings that is the perfection of a finite ring map. For any R-module M, if M⊗_R S is S-flat, then M is R-flat.

items.name: Perfect-group orbit is locally closed
items.statement: For connected affine pfp perfect H acting on separated pfp perfect X and a k-rational point x, H/H_x→X is a locally closed immersion. A general geometric point is treated after its residue-field base change.

items.name: Ramified Witt coefficients
items.statement: Fix a complete mixed-characteristic DVR O with uniformizer ϖ, residue perfect k and Cohen map W(k)→O. Put W_O(R)=W(R)⊗_(W(k))O for perfect k-algebras R, with its ϖ-adic topology.

api.name: Zhu17.G01.construct
api.statement: Construct the coefficient algebra and finite quotients.

api.name: Zhu17.G01.characterise
api.statement: Identify reduction modulo ϖ with R and prove ϖ-torsionfreeness.

api.name: Zhu17.G01.transport
api.statement: Transport perfect k-algebra maps continuously.

uses.how: Provides integral and punctured coefficients.

items.name: Greenberg jets and perfect loops
items.statement: For an affine O-scheme X define L_p^hX(R)=X(W_O(R)/ϖ^h), L_p^+X as the inverse limit; on perfect R define L^hX and L^+X by perfection. For affine F-schemes define LX(R)=X(W_O(R)[1/ϖ]).

api.name: Zhu17.G02.construct
api.statement: Represent finite Greenberg jets by Witt-coordinate equations.

api.name: Zhu17.G02.characterise
api.statement: Compare L^+X with the inverse limit of perfected finite jets.

api.name: Zhu17.G02.transport
api.statement: Preserve open immersions and coefficient-compatible maps.

uses.how: Makes the loop quotient a geometric functor.

items.name: Representability of punctured loops
items.statement: For affine finite-type F-scheme X, LX is represented by an ind-perfect scheme.

items.name: Integral loops as a closed subfunctor
items.statement: For affine finite-type O-scheme X, L^+X→LX_F is closed; loop functors preserve closed immersions in the stated affine setting.

items.name: Congruence subgroups through dilatation
items.statement: For smooth affine G/O, G^(h) is the iterated dilatation at the identity, with L^+G^(h)=ker(L^+G→L^hG) on perfect tests.

api.name: Zhu17.G05.construct
api.statement: Construct the successive dilatations.

api.name: Zhu17.G05.characterise
api.statement: Identify the perfected positive-loop kernel.

api.name: Zhu17.G05.transport
api.statement: Relate successive congruence quotients to additive Lie-algebra groups.

uses.how: Controls finite-level equivariance and pro-unipotent kernels.

items.name: Witt affine Grassmannian
items.statement: For smooth affine G/O, Gr_G is the fpqc sheaf quotient LG/L^+G on perfect k-algebras.

api.name: Zhu17.G06.construct
api.statement: Form the sheaf quotient of the right positive-loop action.

api.name: Zhu17.G06.characterise
api.statement: Identify R-points with G-torsors on W_O(R) trivialized after ϖ-inversion.

api.name: Zhu17.G06.transport
api.statement: Construct base change, group morphism and left-loop action maps.

uses.how: Defines the central geometric object.

items.name: Integral torsor description
items.statement: The quotient Gr_G classifies G-torsors on W_O(R) with a generic trivialization, functorially on perfect R.

items.name: Witt lattices and relative position
items.statement: A lattice is a finite projective W_O(R)-module with a trivialization after ϖ-inversion. Over a perfect field an isogeny has dominant elementary-divisor coweight Inv(β); for families use geometric residue points.

api.name: Zhu17.G08.construct
api.statement: Associate elementary divisors to a field-valued isogeny.

api.name: Zhu17.G08.characterise
api.statement: Detect boundedness by the dominance order on the actual cocharacter lattice.

api.name: Zhu17.G08.transport
api.statement: Transport under residue-field extension and duality, reversing and negating the coweight.

uses.how: Defines bounded Grassmannian loci.

items.name: Minuscule lattice quotient criterion
items.statement: For ω_i=(1^i,0^(n−i)), Inv(E1→E2)=ω_i iff ϖE2⊂E1⊂E2 and E2/E1 is projective over R of rank i, under the perfect-base finite-projective hypotheses.

items.name: Closed relative-position bounds
items.statement: For lattice isogenies over perfect R the locus Inv≤μ is closed and the exact-position locus is open in it.

items.name: Separated lattice quotient
items.statement: The diagonal of the lattice Grassmannian is a closed immersion.

items.name: Cartan orbit classification
items.statement: Over algebraically closed k, L^+G-orbits for split reductive G on Gr_G are indexed by dominant coweights.

items.name: Bounded matrix presentation
items.statement: For GL_n and N≥0 let V_N={(A,t):t det A=ϖ^N}; Gr_N is its perfected positive-loop quotient by GL_n, classifying nonnegative lattices of total colength N.

api.name: Zhu17.G13.construct
api.statement: Construct the matrix-and-inverse-unit presentation.

api.name: Zhu17.G13.characterise
api.statement: Prove the GL_n action is free on perfect tests and identify the quotient.

api.name: Zhu17.G13.transport
api.statement: Compare increasing denominator/colength bounds with all of Gr_GL_n.

uses.how: Produces finite-dimensional bounds.

items.name: Finite-jet stabilizer presentation
items.statement: For h>N, V′_(N,h) imposes determinant coordinates 0 through N−1 zero and the Nth invertible; J consists of pairs (A,γ) with Aγ=A modulo ϖ^h. Gr_(N,h) is the level-h lattice-frame torsor.

api.name: Zhu17.G14.construct
api.statement: Define the finite-jet determinant open and stabilizer scheme.

api.name: Zhu17.G14.characterise
api.statement: Choose a set-theoretic Witt-coordinate lift and identify Gr_(N,h) with J noncanonically.

api.name: Zhu17.G14.transport
api.statement: Show the quotient is independent of the chosen lift.

uses.how: Allows application of the perfect free-action quotient theorem.

items.name: Bounded Grassmannian algebraic space
items.statement: Gr_N is a separated pfp perfect algebraic space.

items.name: Demazure lattice-chain space
items.statement: For a sequence of minuscule or dual-minuscule positions μ•, Gr_(μ•) classifies successive lattice modifications of those positions with a fixed initial lattice.

api.name: Zhu17.G16.construct
api.statement: Construct the iterated relative Grassmannian functor.

api.name: Zhu17.G16.characterise
api.statement: Identify each successive quotient bundle and its rank.

api.name: Zhu17.G16.transport
api.statement: Compose chains and map to their endpoint, with reversed dual-chain compatibility.

uses.how: Resolves bounded loci.

items.name: Projective quotient lifting
items.statement: For a minuscule lattice inclusion E′⊂E, the kernel of E′/ϖ→E/ϖ is projective over R and E′ remains finite projective over W_O(R).

items.name: Proper Demazure tower
items.statement: The minuscule/dual-minuscule chain space is a perfectly proper perfect scheme, given by an iterated Grassmann bundle.

items.name: First two one-step towers
items.statement: For ω1 chains of lengths one and two, the resolution is respectively perfected P^(n−1) and the specified projective bundle P(Ω_(P^(n−1))⊕O), with the paper’s quotient convention.

items.name: Proper convolution and scheme fibres
items.statement: The endpoint map from a minuscule chain to the appropriate bounded Grassmannian is perfectly proper; its fibres are perfect schemes.

items.name: Open isomorphism of the full ω1 resolution
items.statement: The length-N ω1-chain resolution of Gr_N is an isomorphism over Gr_(Nω1).

items.name: Connected boundary fibres
items.statement: The full ω1-chain resolution is surjective, with geometrically connected fibres; over the boundary of Gr_(Nω1), fibres have positive dimension.

items.name: Irreducibility and properness of bounds
items.statement: Gr_N is irreducible and perfectly proper.

items.name: Grassmannian embedding comparison
items.statement: A closed embedding G→GL_n with quasi-affine respectively affine quotient induces a locally closed respectively closed immersion of Grassmannians.

items.name: Weil-restriction comparison
items.statement: For a finite extension of coefficient DVRs, the loop and Grassmannian functors of restriction of scalars agree with the corresponding coefficient-extension functors.

items.name: Iwahori–Weyl and parahoric flag data
items.statement: For a reductive generic fibre choose an apartment and alcove, its Iwahori I, connected Néron torus model and W̃=N(F)/T(O); affine simple reflections and length use that choice.

api.name: Zhu17.G26.construct
api.statement: Construct the chosen alcove, parahorics and normalizer quotient.

api.name: Zhu17.G26.characterise
api.statement: Compare W̃ with the affine Weyl subgroup and length-zero component group.

api.name: Zhu17.G26.transport
api.statement: Transport conjugate alcove choices with their resulting flag functors.

uses.how: Provides flag cells, Kottwitz components and KL indexing.

items.name: Affine flag Schubert cells
items.statement: Iwahori orbits in the perfect affine flag variety are perfected affine spaces of dimension ℓ(w). A simple parahoric quotient is perfected P1.

items.name: Affine flag Demazure resolution
items.statement: A reduced word gives a perfectly proper iterated P1-bundle onto the Schubert closure, with connected fibres.

items.name: Ind-properness theorem
items.statement: For smooth affine G/O the Grassmannian is a separated ind-pfp perfect algebraic space; for reductive G it is ind-perfectly proper.

items.name: Kottwitz connected components
items.statement: Over algebraically closed residue field, π0(LG)≅π0(Gr_G)≅π1(G)_Γ under the Kottwitz map.

items.name: General reductive position bounds
items.statement: For reductive G, relative position ≤μ defines a closed subspace in any family of modifications.

items.name: Orbit dimension and finite model
items.statement: For split reductive G and dominant μ, Gr_μ is perfectly smooth with a smooth quasiprojective finite-type model, of dimension ⟨2ρ,μ⟩; its closure has the same dimension and is perfectly proper.

items.name: Orbit projection to the partial flag
items.statement: Gr_μ maps to the special-fibre partial flag Ḡ/P_μ with perfected affine fibres; for minuscule μ this is an isomorphism.

items.name: Component parity
items.statement: The parity sign on π1(G)_Γ is p(μ)=(-1)^⟨2ρ,μ⟩; the additive degree ε(μ)=(1−p(μ))/2 lies in Z/2.

api.name: Zhu17.G34.construct
api.statement: Descend the sign through the coroot lattice.

api.name: Zhu17.G34.characterise
api.statement: Relate cohomological parity to ε and keep p as a multiplicative sign.

api.name: Zhu17.G34.transport
api.statement: Add component degrees under convolution.

uses.how: Supplies the corrected commutativity sign.

items.name: Constructible coefficients on perfect spaces
items.statement: For separated pfp perfect k-spaces and ℓ invertible in k, define D_c^b(X,Q̄_ℓ) through finite-type models and the étale-topos equivalence; use coherent finite-level coefficient systems.
items.note: The ordinary finite-type theorem has an existing EDC/upstream owner. This item includes a perfect-model extension not yet explicitly closed by that plan, so its status is conservatively missing and its source route extends the same owner.

api.name: Zhu17.E01.construct
api.statement: Construct the model comparison equivalence with Q̄_ℓ coefficients.

api.name: Zhu17.E01.characterise
api.statement: Show Frobenius-twisted refinements give compatible equivalences.

api.name: Zhu17.E01.transport
api.statement: Transport pullback and proper-support pushforward through common models.

uses.how: Supplies all coefficient operations.

items.name: Six operations on perfect pfp spaces
items.statement: The six operations, base change and projection formula on compatible finite-type models descend to separated pfp perfect spaces.
items.note: The ordinary finite-type theorem has an existing EDC/upstream owner. This item includes a perfect-model extension not yet explicitly closed by that plan, so its status is conservatively missing and its source route extends the same owner.

items.name: Verdier biduality
items.statement: Constructible bounded complexes on the stated perfect spaces admit Verdier duality and biduality, with D_Y f_!≅f_*D_X.
items.note: The ordinary finite-type theorem has an existing EDC/upstream owner. This item includes a perfect-model extension not yet explicitly closed by that plan, so its status is conservatively missing and its source route extends the same owner.

items.name: Perverse t-structure
items.statement: The middle-perverse conditions defined by geometric-point stalk/costalk dimension bounds form a t-structure on D_c^b of a pfp perfect space.
items.note: The ordinary finite-type theorem has an existing EDC/upstream owner. This item includes a perfect-model extension not yet explicitly closed by that plan, so its status is conservatively missing and its source route extends the same owner.

items.name: Decomposition theorem
items.statement: A proper map of the finite-type models in use decomposes a pure shifted intersection complex into semisimple perverse summands after passing to Q̄_ℓ.
items.note: The ordinary finite-type theorem has an existing EDC/upstream owner. This item includes a perfect-model extension not yet explicitly closed by that plan, so its status is conservatively missing and its source route extends the same owner.

items.name: Hyperbolic localization
items.statement: For a compatible G_m action on a finite-type model, Braden’s attracting and repelling functors agree with the prescribed compact/ordinary support conventions.

items.name: Middle intersection complex
items.statement: For a geometrically irreducible pfp perfect space X of dimension d with a smooth dense open j:U→X, IC_X=j_!*Q̄_ℓ[d]; a Tate half-normalization requires a separate choice.
items.note: The ordinary finite-type theorem has an existing EDC/upstream owner. This item includes a perfect-model extension not yet explicitly closed by that plan, so its status is conservatively missing and its source route extends the same owner.

api.name: Zhu17.E05.construct
api.statement: Form the perverse intermediate extension.

api.name: Zhu17.E05.characterise
api.statement: Characterize it by no boundary subobject or quotient and its restriction Q̄_ℓ[d].

api.name: Zhu17.E05.transport
api.statement: Compare dense smooth opens and model changes.

uses.how: Fixes shifts before stalk KL comparisons.

items.name: Fundamental classes and top components
items.statement: Use the dualizing complex to define Borel–Moore homology; after fixing geometric components and trace orientations, top compact cohomology has a basis indexed by top-dimensional geometric irreducible components, with Tate twists retained.
items.note: The ordinary finite-type theorem has an existing EDC/upstream owner. This item includes a perfect-model extension not yet explicitly closed by that plan, so its status is conservatively missing and its source route extends the same owner.

api.name: Zhu17.E07.construct
api.statement: Construct classes from smooth dense opens with their purity orientation.

api.name: Zhu17.E07.characterise
api.statement: Identify top cohomology componentwise, not by an unconditional scalar trace.

api.name: Zhu17.E07.transport
api.statement: Prove proper pushforward with degrees and smooth pullback with dimension shifts.

uses.how: Produces cycle bases once the orientation gate is closed.

items.name: Frobenius trace function
items.statement: For a Weil complex on a separated pfp perfect X/F_q, transport the existing finite-type Frobenius trace function through a model: at x∈X(F_(q^r)), take the alternating trace of Frobenius^r. The imported proper-support trace theorem identifies f_! with fibrewise summation.
items.note: TraceFormula and EllAdicRealization are existing upstream owners. This item adds only the perfect-model comparison; it does not re-plan their ordinary trace construction.

api.name: Zhu17.E08.construct
api.statement: Construct the function at a specified extension degree r.

api.name: Zhu17.E08.characterise
api.statement: Prove additivity, shifts and Tate-twist factors.

api.name: Zhu17.E08.transport
api.statement: Compare f_! with summing over rational points of each fibre.

uses.how: Relates geometry to Hecke coefficients and twisted traces.

items.name: Finite-level equivariant coefficients
items.statement: For perfect affine H acting on X through a pfp quotient with finite-codimensional pro-unipotent kernel, define equivariant perverse sheaves and cohomology through that quotient.
items.note: The equivariant perfect-space extension is missing; the existing EDC.5 perverse and EDC.0/6 coefficient interfaces supply its generic inputs. EDC.7 is not an early equivariance prerequisite.

api.name: Zhu17.E10.construct
api.statement: Construct descent data satisfying the cocycle identity.

api.name: Zhu17.E10.characterise
api.statement: Compare quotients by smaller normal pro-unipotent kernels.

api.name: Zhu17.E10.transport
api.statement: Pull back equivariant complexes along equivariant maps.

uses.how: Defines Satake equivariance without an infinite-dimensional classifying space shortcut.

items.name: Equivariant torsor descent
items.statement: For a free normal subgroup K⊂H with represented quotient, equivariant perverse sheaves descend along the K-torsor with the required relative-dimension shift.

items.name: Trivial connected and unipotent kernels
items.statement: A connected trivially acting kernel does not change equivariant perverse sheaves; if it is unipotent it also does not change equivariant cohomology.

items.name: Equivariant coefficient ring
items.statement: For connected affine H with reductive quotient G, R_H=H*(BH,Q̄_ℓ)≅R_G; for reductive G it is the Weyl-invariant symmetric algebra on torus characters with generators in degree two.

api.name: Zhu17.E13.construct
api.statement: Construct classifying-space cohomology using finite-dimensional Stiefel approximations.

api.name: Zhu17.E13.characterise
api.statement: Identify restriction R_G→R_T with the Weyl invariants.

api.name: Zhu17.E13.transport
api.statement: Relate characters, Chern classes and parabolic restriction.

uses.how: Controls the two actions on equivariant cohomology.

items.name: Semisimple Satake category
items.statement: Over algebraically closed k, Sat_G is the filtered category of L^+G-equivariant perverse Q̄_ℓ sheaves supported on bounded closed unions of Gr_G orbits.

api.name: Zhu17.S01.construct
api.statement: Construct the bounded equivariant categories and closed-extension transition functors.

api.name: Zhu17.S01.characterise
api.statement: Identify simple objects IC_μ using connected orbit stabilizers.

api.name: Zhu17.S01.transport
api.statement: Extend scalars and transport compatible integral group isomorphisms.

uses.how: Defines the rational Satake category.

items.name: Satake semisimplicity
items.statement: Sat_G is semisimple with simple objects IC_μ indexed by dominant coweights.

items.name: Twisted convolution product
items.statement: The twisted product Gr_G×̃Gr_G=LG×^(L^+G)Gr_G carries endpoint multiplication m; bounded factors carry descended external products A1⊠̃A2 and convolution m_!(A1⊠̃A2).

api.name: Zhu17.S03.construct
api.statement: Construct the contracted product and descend the external coefficient complex.

api.name: Zhu17.S03.characterise
api.statement: Compare the full twisted space with endpoint pairs, retaining bounded twisted incidence conditions.

api.name: Zhu17.S03.transport
api.statement: Construct associativity through the three-step quotient diagram.

uses.how: Defines geometric multiplication.

items.name: Semi-infinite orbit and weight functor
items.statement: For a chosen Borel T⊂B with unipotent U, S_λ=LU·ϖ^λ is the semi-infinite orbit. Set CT_λ(A)=H_c^⟨2ρ,λ⟩(S_λ,A) after the concentration theorem.

api.name: Zhu17.S04.construct
api.statement: Construct the locally closed orbit using a quasi-affine U quotient and the attracting action.

api.name: Zhu17.S04.characterise
api.statement: Compare opposite repellers and the coweight-indexed support filtration.

api.name: Zhu17.S04.transport
api.statement: Transport by torus characters and Levi restriction.

uses.how: Connects geometry to weights of the dual group.

items.name: Semi-infinite closure order
items.statement: The closure of S_λ is the union of S_ν with ν≤λ in the appropriate coroot order.

items.name: Semi-infinite product coordinates
items.statement: The full twisted LU-orbit product has an explicit ordinary-product description with partial-sum indices; the intersections with bounded Schubert factors remain twisted incidence spaces.

items.name: MV intersection dimension
items.statement: Whenever S_λ∩Gr_μ is nonempty, its dimension is ⟨ρ,λ+μ⟩; its maximal-dimensional components are counted by the λ-weight multiplicity in the dual highest-weight representation V_μ.

items.name: Quasi-minuscule parahoric resolution
items.statement: For the dominant short coroot θ, take the parahorics Q_r along the segment rθ for r=0,1/4,1/2,3/4,1. Their contracted quotient gives a P1-bundle resolution of Gr_θ∪Gr_0.

api.name: Zhu17.Q01.construct
api.statement: Construct each Q_r by root-valuation inequalities and the adjacent intersections.

api.name: Zhu17.Q01.characterise
api.statement: Identify the P1 bundle and its exceptional flag divisor.

api.name: Zhu17.Q01.transport
api.statement: Compute the negative Bruhat cells meeting the zero semi-infinite fibre.

uses.how: Provides the independent initial case for perversity.

items.name: Minuscule and quasi-minuscule weight concentration
items.statement: For a minimal nonzero dominant coweight μ, H_c^i(S_λ,IC_μ)=0 unless i=⟨2ρ,λ⟩.

items.name: Zero quasi-minuscule multiplicity
items.statement: The zero weight in the quasi-minuscule intersection complex has dimension equal to the number of short simple coroots in the specified orbit; its cycle classes come from the negative cells indexed by those coroots.

items.name: Minimal convolution dimension bound
items.statement: For a sequence of minimal nonzero dominant coweights, the convolution fibres over Gr_λ have dimension at most ⟨ρ,Σμ_i−λ⟩.

items.name: Minimal convolution is perverse
items.statement: Convolution of the minimal IC objects is perverse.

items.name: Generation by minimal objects
items.statement: Sat_G is the idempotent completion of the additive monoidal subcategory generated by the minimal nonzero IC objects (and component/unit objects as required).

items.name: Concentration for minimal products
items.statement: For a convolution of minimal IC objects, semi-infinite compact cohomology is concentrated in the total weight degree.

items.name: General convolution perversity
items.statement: Convolution preserves Sat_G.

items.name: General convolution semismallness
items.statement: For dominant μ• and λ, every nonempty fibre of the bounded convolution over Gr_λ has dimension at most ⟨ρ,Σμ_i−λ⟩.

items.name: Convolution multiplicity cycles
items.statement: The multiplicity of IC_λ in IC_μ1⋆…⋆IC_μn is the top compact cohomology of the appropriate open-stratum convolution fibre, with basis its maximal components.

items.name: Weight concentration for all Satake objects
items.statement: For every A∈Sat_G, H_c^i(S_λ,A) vanishes unless i=⟨2ρ,λ⟩.

items.name: Weight cycle basis
items.statement: For IC_μ, CT_λ is the component space of S_λ∩Gr_μ; the unshifted open-orbit compact degree is ⟨2ρ,λ+μ⟩.

items.name: Total weights equal ordinary cohomology
items.statement: The direct sum of CT_λ(A) identifies canonically with H*(Gr_G,A); these functors are exact and the total functor is faithful.

items.name: Equivariant cohomology bimodule
items.statement: For A∈Sat_G, finite-jet torsor presentations give H*_(L+G)(A) commuting left and right R_G actions, independent of the sufficiently deep congruence level.

api.name: Zhu17.S14.construct
api.statement: Construct both coefficient-ring actions from the two frame torsors.

api.name: Zhu17.S14.characterise
api.statement: Compare levels through pro-unipotent kernels.

api.name: Zhu17.S14.transport
api.statement: Attach the tensor-over-R_G map to convolution.

uses.how: Builds a monoidal fibre functor without fusion.

items.name: Equivariant Künneth for convolution
items.statement: H_eq*(A⋆B)≅H_eq*(A)⊗_(R_G)H_eq*(B), compatibly with associativity and both outer actions.

items.name: Equality of the two R_G actions
items.statement: The two coefficient-ring actions on H_eq*(A) agree for every Satake object A.

items.name: Monoidal ordinary cohomology
items.statement: Equivariant cohomology is finite projective over R_G and augmentation R_G→Q̄_ℓ yields a monoidal structure on H*:Sat_G→Vect_(Q̄_ℓ).

items.name: Normalized classical Satake transform
items.statement: For the split unramified group and hyperspecial K, the spherical convolution algebra maps isomorphically to Weyl-invariant functions on the dual torus by the normalized constant term, with Haar vol(U(O))=1 and the specified q^⟨ρ,λ⟩ factor.

items.name: Lusztig–Kato weight formula
items.statement: The spherical basis and the irreducible dual-group characters are related by the normalized inverse-q intersection/KL polynomials used in the point-count expansion of S_λ∩Gr_μ.

items.name: Affine Hecke and twisted involution module
items.statement: For an affine Coxeter system (W_a,S), involutive diagram automorphism ⋄ and the specified equal-parameter ring, use its generic Hecke algebra, ordinary KL basis and the Lusztig–Vogan module on ⋄-twisted involutions.

api.name: Zhu17.H03.construct
api.statement: Import the shared generic Hecke presentation and construct the twisted module with its bar involution.

api.name: Zhu17.H03.characterise
api.statement: Define ordinary and twisted KL polynomials by triangularity and bar invariance with explicit q/v conversion.

api.name: Zhu17.H03.transport
api.statement: Transport diagram automorphisms and the length-zero conjugation defining ⋄.

uses.how: Hosts the numerical identity reused in mixed characteristic.

items.name: Longest double-coset involution indexing
items.statement: Write W̃=W_a⋊Ω; for ω∈Ω with ω*=ω⁻¹ put ⋄=Ad(ω)∘*. The elements indexing the theorem are longest representatives of (W_J,W_(J^⋄)) double cosets that are ⋄-twisted involutions.

api.name: Zhu17.H04.construct
api.statement: Construct the twisted automorphism and its order-two proof.

api.name: Zhu17.H04.characterise
api.statement: Identify the finite-parabolic longest double-coset representatives.

api.name: Zhu17.H04.transport
api.statement: Compare the coweight indexing with the corresponding Schubert stalks.

uses.how: Prevents overgeneralizing P^σ(q)=P(−q).

items.name: Equal-characteristic geometric Satake input
items.statement: For a reductive group over the equal-characteristic algebraically closed base, the classical geometric Satake theorem gives the normalized symmetric tensor equivalence and its cohomology fibre functor.

items.name: Equal-characteristic opposition sign
items.statement: In the equal-characteristic setting, the normalized opposition acts by (−1)^j on IH^(2j) of a Schubert variety, with the corresponding normalized stalk sign.

items.name: Lusztig–Yun twisted polynomial identity
items.statement: For exactly the longest double-coset elements and twisted automorphism of H04, P^(σ,⋄)_(x,y)(q)=P_(x,y)(−q).

items.name: Mixed-characteristic KL stalk realization
items.statement: Ordinary and twisted KL polynomials in H03 realize dimensions and involution traces of normalized even IC stalks of the mixed-characteristic affine flag Schubert spaces at the specified strata.

items.name: Opposite Grassmannian category
items.statement: The opposite quotient Gr_G^op=L^+G\LG has its finite-level equivariant IC category and convolution; inversion reverses ordered modifications.

api.name: Zhu17.O01.construct
api.statement: Construct opposite finite quotients and their common torsor correspondence.

api.name: Zhu17.O01.characterise
api.statement: Identify the pulled-back IC objects by the finite-level argument.

api.name: Zhu17.O01.transport
api.statement: Build the equivalence Id′ and its monoidal structure.

uses.how: Defines the comparison used in Gelfand’s trick.

items.name: Finite-level opposite IC comparison
items.statement: The two finite-level pullbacks of each IC_μ agree with the indicated shifts, giving a monoidal equivalence between Satake and opposite Satake.

items.name: Canonical opposite stalk and costalk maps
items.statement: The opposite equivalence gives compatible maps on normalized stalks and costalks; the latter is constructed using i!C=D_S i*D_XC with all shifts and twists.

items.name: Pinned opposition anti-involution
items.statement: Let θ′ be the pinned automorphism acting as −w0 on coweights and let θ=θ′∘inverse. It is an anti-involution of LG, inducing an order-reversing tensor pullback to the opposite category.

api.name: Zhu17.O04.construct
api.statement: Construct the pinned group automorphism and compose with inversion.

api.name: Zhu17.O04.characterise
api.statement: Prove θ²=id and θ(gh)=θ(h)θ(g).

api.name: Zhu17.O04.transport
api.statement: Compare its action on coweight strata and reversed convolution.

uses.how: Supplies the reversal map on cohomology.

items.name: Normalized IC involution
items.statement: Choose a square root i of −1 in Q̄_ℓ. Normalize N_μ:θ*IC_μ≅IC_μ by the identity on the open stratum and use the source phase M_μ=(−1)^−⟨ρ,μ⟩N_μ, interpreted via i.

api.name: Zhu17.O05.construct
api.statement: Construct the unique open-normalized simple-object isomorphism.

api.name: Zhu17.O05.characterise
api.statement: Separate the N involution from its degree-dependent M phase.

api.name: Zhu17.O05.transport
api.statement: Extend through semisimple sums and compare changes of the chosen square root.

uses.how: Defines the natural transformation entering the commutativity map.

items.name: Monoidal opposite cohomology comparison
items.statement: The comparison γ:H*≅H*Id′ respects the tensor structures from equivariant bimodules.

items.name: Reversal comparison on cohomology
items.statement: The map δ:H*≅H*θ* is compatible with reversed ordered tensor products and the graded interchange signs.

items.name: Open-orbit opposition sign
items.statement: On the even cohomology of Gr_μ, the normalized open-orbit involution acts as (−1)^j in degree 2j.

items.name: Stalk opposition sign
items.statement: On each normalized IC stalk even-degree part, the involution acts by the scalar (−1)^j.

items.name: Global intersection-cohomology sign
items.statement: On IH^(2j)(Gr_≤μ), Θ_μ acts by (−1)^j.

items.name: Graded cohomology phase
items.statement: The normalized natural transformation Θ on H^j(A) is multiplication by i^j with the source’s chosen phase convention.

items.name: Rational commutativity constraint
items.statement: The opposite equivalence, θ and the normalized maps define c′_(A,B). For component-homogeneous A,B put c_(A,B)=(-1)^(ε(A)ε(B))c′_(A,B), using additive parity ε.

api.name: Zhu17.O12.construct
api.statement: Construct the reversed-convolution isomorphism from the three natural transformations.

api.name: Zhu17.O12.characterise
api.statement: Show its normalized cohomology is the ordinary vector-space flip.

api.name: Zhu17.O12.transport
api.statement: Extend by component decompositions and prove independence of i.

uses.how: Constructs symmetry without substituting a fusion proof.

items.name: Symmetry and hexagon
items.statement: The corrected commutativity constraint is symmetric and satisfies the unit and hexagon axioms.

items.name: Neutral Tannakian reconstruction
items.statement: For a Q̄_ℓ-linear abelian rigid symmetric tensor category with an exact faithful fibre functor and scalar endomorphisms of the unit, construct its tensor-automorphism affine group scheme and the representation equivalence.

api.name: Zhu17.T01.construct
api.statement: Construct the coend/Hopf algebra from the category and fibre functor.

api.name: Zhu17.T01.characterise
api.statement: Identify its points with tensor automorphisms, reusing the pinned known-Hopf comparison afterward.

api.name: Zhu17.T01.transport
api.statement: Prove reconstruction and naturality for tensor functors.

uses.how: Supplies the general categorical theorem once, through MC.6.

items.name: Satake rigidity and neutral structure
items.statement: With the symmetry above, Sat_G and H* form a neutral Tannakian category; duals use Verdier duality and inversion with the fixed coefficient convention.

items.name: Rational Tannakian reductivity
items.statement: The reconstructed Satake group is connected reductive over Q̄_ℓ.

items.name: Torus Satake equivalence
items.statement: For a torus T, Sat_T with convolution is the category of finite-support X_*(T)-graded finite-dimensional vector spaces and reconstructs the dual torus.

items.name: Tensor constant term
items.statement: The total weight functor CT from Sat_G to Sat_T is a tensor functor, compatibly with its identification with H*.

items.name: Dual root datum identification
items.statement: The weight torus is maximal in the Satake group, its weight filtration determines a Borel, and its based root datum is dual to that of G.
items.note: The rational specialization belongs to the existing identification stage, but Zhu does not prove its integral recovery target. The rational Gelfand route supplies an alternative symmetry input only.

items.name: Mixed-characteristic rational geometric Satake
items.statement: For the reductive O-group over algebraically closed residue field, Sat_G is equivalent as a symmetric monoidal Q̄_ℓ-linear category to finite-dimensional representations of the dual group, with H* the forgetful fibre functor.

items.name: Closed and exact affine Deligne–Lusztig spaces
items.statement: For unramified reductive G, b∈G(L), dominant μ and Frobenius σ, let X_≤μ(b)={gK:Inv(g⁻¹bσ(g))≤μ}; X_μ(b) is its exact-position stratum. These are perfect locally closed/closed subspaces of Gr_G with the inherited bounded presentations.

api.name: Zhu17.D01.construct
api.statement: Form the relative-position pullback along the Frobenius graph.

api.name: Zhu17.D01.characterise
api.statement: Separate the closed bound from its exact open stratum.

api.name: Zhu17.D01.transport
api.statement: Transport by σ-conjugating b and by compatible coefficient extension.

uses.how: Defines the spaces whose dimensions are computed.

items.name: Newton point and defect
items.statement: For b∈G(L), retain its dominant Newton point ν_b, Kottwitz invariant and σ-centralizer J_b; def_G(b)=rk_F(G)−rk_F(J_b).

api.name: Zhu17.D02.construct
api.statement: Construct J_b by the equation g⁻¹bσ(g)=b.

api.name: Zhu17.D02.characterise
api.statement: Compare Newton and Kottwitz invariants under σ-conjugacy.

api.name: Zhu17.D02.transport
api.statement: Compute defect under adjoint, Levi and restriction-of-scalars reductions.

uses.how: Supplies the dimension correction.

items.name: Basic-Levi reduction
items.statement: The ADLV dimension problem reduces from b to a basic class in the Levi centralizing ν_b, with the corresponding root/weight correction and nonemptiness constraints.

items.name: Superbasic adjoint reduction
items.statement: The basic dimension problem reduces through adjoint simple factors to the superbasic case, whose relevant factors are restrictions of scalars of PGL_n.

items.name: Equal-characteristic comparison for the basic model
items.statement: The finite-type model used in the superbasic reduction admits the stated equal-characteristic comparison, sufficient for the point-count/dimension argument; the comparison used here is not asserted an isomorphism of group schemes.

items.name: Iterated affine Deligne–Lusztig space
items.statement: For a coweight sequence μ•, pull the convolution correspondence (pr1,m) back along the graph of bσ to obtain X_(μ•)(b), equivalently a cyclic chain of bounded modifications.

api.name: Zhu17.D06.construct
api.statement: Construct the graph pullback with its chain description.

api.name: Zhu17.D06.characterise
api.statement: Stratify the endpoint position by exact dominant λ≤Σμ_i.

api.name: Zhu17.D06.transport
api.statement: Compare its map to X_≤Σμ_i(b) with convolution fibres.

uses.how: Turns restriction of scalars into convolution.

items.name: Ordered Frobenius norm
items.statement: For unramified E/F of degree d and b=(b0,…,b_(d−1)) in the split factors of Res_(E/F)H, set Nm(b)=b0σ(b1)…σ^(d−1)(b_(d−1)).

api.name: Zhu17.D07.construct
api.statement: Construct the ordered product with the chosen embedding cycle.

api.name: Zhu17.D07.characterise
api.statement: Show σ-conjugacy maps to σ^d-conjugacy by telescoping.

api.name: Zhu17.D07.transport
api.statement: Compare changing the initial embedding by the specified cyclic conjugation.

uses.how: Identifies the correct superbasic target.

items.name: Restriction-of-scalars iterated comparison
items.statement: The ADLV for Res_(E/F)GL_n identifies with the iterated ADLV for GL_n over E, with ordered norm and the σ-twisted coweight sequence.

items.name: Norm Newton pairing
items.statement: Under D08 the sum of root pairings and the Newton pairing transform as in Lemma3.7, with all d factors and σ-twisted coweights included.

items.name: Norm defect comparison
items.statement: The σ-centralizer under restriction of scalars identifies with the restriction of the σ^d-centralizer of Nm(b), and the corresponding defects agree.

items.name: Stratified semismall upper bound
items.statement: For each exact endpoint stratum X_λ(b), the inverse image in the iterated ADLV has dimension at most dim X_λ(b)+⟨ρ,Σμ_i−λ⟩. Taking the maximum over the finite λ set gives the upper bound over X_≤Σμ_i(b).

items.name: Top-stratum lower bound
items.statement: When the exact top ADLV stratum is nonempty with the required full dimension, its inverse image under convolution gives the matching lower dimension bound; verify this condition in the superbasic GL_n argument.

items.name: Superbasic restriction-of-scalars dimension
items.statement: For the nonempty ADLV of Res_(E/F)GL_n in the superbasic case, dim X_≤μ(b)=⟨ρ,μ−ν_b⟩−def_G(b)/2.

items.name: Affine Deligne–Lusztig dimension theorem
items.statement: For unramified reductive G and nonempty X_≤μ(b), dim X_≤μ(b)=⟨ρ,μ−ν_b⟩−def_G(b)/2.

items.name: Contravariant Dieudonné module over perfect rings
items.statement: For a p-divisible group over perfect k-algebra R, its contravariant Dieudonné module is finite projective over W(R), with semilinear F,V and FV=VF=p, in the scope of Gabber’s equivalence used by Zhu.

api.name: Zhu17.R01.construct
api.statement: Apply the perfect-ring classification with its exact finiteness hypotheses.

api.name: Zhu17.R01.characterise
api.statement: Recover the group from the Dieudonné module and integral F,V conditions.

api.name: Zhu17.R01.transport
api.statement: Transport quasi-isogenies contravariantly and preserve base change.

uses.how: Makes the perfect RZ comparison functorial on test rings.

items.name: Hodge-type framed datum
items.statement: Fix p>2, unramified G/Z_p, minuscule μ and a faithful lattice representation with μ-weights 0,1 and tensor stabilizer G. Choose b and a Dieudonné framing whose Hodge filtration is adapted to that μ-convention.

api.name: Zhu17.R02.construct
api.statement: Construct the tensor frame and the two-step filtration.

api.name: Zhu17.R02.characterise
api.statement: Express the F,V conditions and the adapted-frame constraint.

api.name: Zhu17.R02.transport
api.statement: Transport b, tensors and filtration together under change of frame.

uses.how: Prevents an unproved simultaneous framing assertion.

items.name: Hodge-type Rapoport–Zink moduli
items.statement: On the specified formally smooth nilpotent W-bases, classify deformations X of the framing p-divisible group, a quasi-isogeny X0→X on the special fibre and filtered crystalline Tate tensors whose isomorphism functor is a G-torsor.

api.name: Zhu17.R03.construct
api.statement: Construct the deformation groupoid and tensor conditions.

api.name: Zhu17.R03.characterise
api.statement: Compare its GL realization with the ambient RZ functor.

api.name: Zhu17.R03.transport
api.statement: Transport a faithful tensor presentation using the cited independence theorem.

uses.how: Defines the integral moduli consumer.

items.name: Hodge-type RZ representability
items.statement: For the unramified Hodge-type datum with p>2, the functor is represented by a closed formally smooth RZ formal subscheme with the stated k-point ADLV identification.

items.name: GL perfect RZ comparison
items.statement: For GL_n, the perfected reduced special fibre of the RZ space identifies functorially with X_≤μ(b).

items.name: Hodge perfect RZ comparison
items.statement: For the stated Hodge-type datum, the perfected reduced RZ special fibre is canonically isomorphic to X_≤μ(b).

items.name: Hodge RZ dimension
items.statement: For a nonempty Hodge-type RZ space under these hypotheses, its reduced special-fibre dimension is ⟨ρ,μ−ν_b⟩−def_G(b)/2.

items.name: Determinant line on a modification chain
items.statement: For a positive minuscule step E′⊂E put L(E′,E)=det_R(E/E′); for the paper’s negative step use its separately specified quotient convention. Tensor the step lines to obtain L̃_det on the positive full-chain resolution.

api.name: Zhu17.B01.construct
api.statement: Construct each finite-projective quotient determinant and the tensor product along a chain.

api.name: Zhu17.B01.characterise
api.statement: Compare refinements of a positive filtration through exact determinant identities.

api.name: Zhu17.B01.transport
api.statement: Transport the line and its frame-change isomorphisms under base change.

uses.how: Connects Zhu’s line to the later BS support determinant.

items.name: Ordinary cohomology injectivity for the resolution
items.statement: For the full length-N GL_n resolution π:Gr̃_N→Gr_N, π*:H*(Gr_N,k̄,Q̄_ℓ)→H*(Gr̃_N,k̄,Q̄_ℓ) is injective.

items.name: Descended first Chern class
items.statement: The first Chern class of L̃_det lies in the image of pullback from the bounded Grassmannian, in the stated rational coefficient cohomology.

items.name: Basepoint freeness implies determinant descent
items.statement: If Γ(Gr̃_N,L̃_det) is basepoint free, then the unique line L_det on Gr_N pulling back to L̃_det exists, and is given by π_*L̃_det.

items.name: Determinant descent and projectivity resolved later
items.statement: ConjecturesI andII of this paper are proved by Bhatt–Scholze17: the determinant line descends and gives projective deperfections of the bounded Witt Grassmannian.

items.name: Exact quasi-isogeny category
items.statement: Use the exact category of triples (M,N,β) of finite projective W(R)-modules with β:M[1/p]≅N[1/p], with the specified degreewise exact sequences. Its K-theory is the object of RemarkB.3’s determinant question.

api.name: Zhu17.B06.construct
api.statement: Construct the triple category and exact sequences.

api.name: Zhu17.B06.characterise
api.statement: Compare its relative/support K-theory with the finite-length quotient description when β is integral.

api.name: Zhu17.B06.transport
api.statement: Transport triples and exact sequences along perfect-ring base change.

uses.how: Reuses the shared support K-theory route instead of inventing a separate K spectrum.

items.name: Canonical weakly normal orbit model
items.statement: Choose the smooth finite-type orbit model Gr′_μ from its finite-jet quotient. Its function fields specify via A.15 a weakly normal proper model Gr′_≤μ of the perfect closure.

api.name: Zhu17.B07.construct
api.statement: Construct the model from the prescribed orbit function fields.

api.name: Zhu17.B07.characterise
api.statement: Identify its perfection and dense open orbit model.

api.name: Zhu17.B07.transport
api.statement: Compare model changes after a finite Frobenius twist.

uses.how: Keeps canonical deperfections distinct from arbitrary projective models.

items.name: Truncated determinant complete intersection
items.statement: For h>N, V′_(N,h) has dimension n²h−N and is a local complete intersection, being cut out by the first N determinant coordinates on the indicated open affine space.

items.name: Normality of the determinant model
items.statement: The scheme V′_(N,h) is normal.

items.name: Canonical models need twisted transition maps
items.statement: For λ<μ, the perfect closed inclusion Gr_≤λ→Gr_≤μ descends after a Frobenius twist of the chosen source model, but that descended map need not be a closed immersion.

items.name: OE-linear isogeny-chain moduli
items.statement: Over k=F̄_p fix h≥N, the unramified E/Q_p of degree 2h with embeddings τ_i=σ^iτ_0, and X0 of height 2hn, dimension hn and signature (0^h,n^h). M_(N,h) classifies OE-linear isogeny chains X0→…→XN: Xi has signature (1^i,0^(h−i),n^(h−i),(n−1)^i); degφ_i=p^(2i−1); dφ_i vanishes on τ_0,…,τ_(h−1), and the dual differential vanishes on τ_h,…,τ_(2h−1).

api.name: Zhu17.B11.construct
api.statement: Construct the chain functor with all four signature/degree/differential conditions.

api.name: Zhu17.B11.characterise
api.statement: Prove the kernels lie in p-torsion and identify the universal extension bundle.

api.name: Zhu17.B11.transport
api.statement: Truncate chains and compare the τ-component Dieudonné maps after perfection.

uses.how: Gives a moduli interpretation of the canonical resolution model.

items.name: Projective tower of isogeny chains
items.statement: For 0≤i<h, M_(i+1,h)=P(E_i) over M_(i,h), where E_i is the rank-n τ0 component of the dual Lie algebra of the universal vector extension. Consequently M_(N,h) is smooth projective.

items.name: Canonical resolution model comparison
items.statement: After choosing D(X0)_τ0≅W(k)^n, the canonical weakly normal model of the full length-N resolution is isomorphic to M_(N,h).

items.name: Hodge determinant on the chain model
items.statement: On M_(N,h), put ω_(XN,τj)=det((Lie XN)^*_(τj)) and L̃′_det=⊗_(i=1)^N ω_(XN,τ_(−i))^(−p^i).

api.name: Zhu17.B14.construct
api.statement: Construct each τ-component determinant and the displayed tensor power.

api.name: Zhu17.B14.characterise
api.statement: Compare the line with its Frobenius pullbacks and the universal Dieudonné quotients.

api.name: Zhu17.B14.transport
api.statement: Transport along chain-moduli base change.

uses.how: Makes the precise determinant normalization a separate comparison.

items.name: Hodge-line comparison
items.statement: Under the perfection isomorphism of B.8, L̃_det is the pullback of L̃′_det on M_(N,h).

items.name: Rank-two quadratic-cone chart
items.statement: For p>2 let U=Spec k[x,y,z]/(x²−yz). On perfect tests form A=[[p+[x],−[y]],[[z],p−[x]]], with det A=p², and map its lattice to Gr_2 for GL2.

api.name: Zhu17.B16.construct
api.statement: Construct the Witt matrix from cone coordinates.

api.name: Zhu17.B16.characterise
api.statement: Verify det A=p² using multiplicativity and [−1]=−1.

api.name: Zhu17.B16.transport
api.statement: Compare the chart with the finite-jet quotient and change of frame.

uses.how: Makes the smallest singular chart explicit.

items.name: Rank-two resolution model
items.statement: The length-two GL2 resolution is the perfection of P(O(1)⊕O(−1)) over P1, with a noncanonical splitting of the underlying rank-two extension.

items.name: Finite Witt matrix factorization
items.statement: On the specified open finite-Witt matrix locus in LemmaB.11, every matrix X factors uniquely as X=A g with A from the cone chart and g invertible, with the determinant-normalizing unit taken in the correct inverse convention.

items.name: Open cone chart and scheme representability
items.statement: U_perf embeds as an open subspace in Gr_2 for GL2,p>2. Together with the smooth open orbit it covers Gr_2, so this bounded perfect algebraic space is a scheme.
items.locator: Lemma B.10 and the paragraph before it

items.name: Rank-two determinant extension
items.statement: In this rank-two length-two example, the determinant line extends from the smooth open orbit by the indicated j_* construction and agrees on the cone chart.

items.name: Chern classes on perfect spaces
items.statement: For a vector bundle E on a pfp perfect space, construct c_i(E) from the Kummer first Chern class and the projective-bundle relation, then pass to normalized rational coefficients.

api.name: Zhu17.E14.construct
api.statement: Construct c1 from the Kummer boundary and c_i from the tautological projective-bundle relation.

api.name: Zhu17.E14.characterise
api.statement: Compare with a finite-type bundle model under its specified pullback.

api.name: Zhu17.E14.transport
api.statement: Prove Whitney sum, base-change and character-torsor compatibility.

uses.how: Makes the source of degree-two generators explicit.

items.name: Embedding into the GL_n Grassmannian
items.statement: If ρ: G → GL_n is a linear representation with GL_n/G quasi-affine, then Gr_G → Gr_{GL_n} is a locally closed embedding; if GL_n/G is affine, it is a closed embedding.

items.name: The open-orbit map Θ_μ is an involution
items.statement: The map Θ_μ is an involution.

items.name: Conjecture III (statement only)
items.statement: The weakly normal proper model Gr′_≤μ is normal and Cohen–Macaulay. Not proved; Lemma B.4 is the evidence given.

items.name: Conjecture IV (statement only)
items.statement: The line bundle L̃′_det on M_(N,h) is semi-ample. Not proved; with Proposition B.2 it would imply Conjecture I (which Bhatt–Scholze 2017 prove).
